chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'How is the greeting to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at his grave?'

He said: 'Peace be upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Peace be upon you, O beloved of Allah. Peace be upon you, O choice of Allah. Peace be upon you, O trustee of Allah. I bear witness that you have been sincere to your community, and you strove in the path of Allah, and you worshipped Him until certainty came to you. So may Allah reward you with the best reward a prophet has received for his community.
O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, with the best blessings You sent upon Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy, Glorious.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to greet the Prophet Muhammad at his grave according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the recommended etiquette for visiting the Prophet’s grave, emphasizing direct address with honorific titles such as 'Habib Allah' and 'Amin Allah'. It highlights the theological concept of the Prophet’s lifelong devotion until death ('al-Yaqin') and links the supplication for his reward to the broader tradition of blessing the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the Shia practice of combining salawat with specific du'a during ziyarat.
